Slavish

SLAY-vish · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Slavish is submissive or unoriginal.

The student's essay was a slavish summary of the textbook, with not a single original idea of her own.

Worked Example

Critics praised the remake for avoiding a slavish copy of the original, adding real new choices instead.

A 'slavish copy' would follow the original with no independent thought at all -- exactly the blind, unoriginal imitation slavish describes.

How Slavish Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

servile

servile: excessively obedient

unoriginal

unoriginal: lacking independent thought or creativity

Antonyms

independent

independent: free from outside control or influence

innovative

innovative: introducing new ideas or methods

How Strong Is It? — derivative → slavish → robotic

derivative vs. slavish

derivative vs. slavish: A derivative style is simply based on someone else's; a slavish one copies so closely it shows no independent thought at all.

robotic vs. slavish

robotic vs. slavish: Robotic copying takes slavish even further, suggesting there is no human judgment left in the process at all, just mechanical repetition.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of slavish.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — slav

root — slav: slave (Middle English (slave))

suffix — -ish

suffix — -ish: having the quality of (English)

Put it together

Put it together: Slave plus the adjective-forming -ish gives 'having the quality of a slave' -- slavish behavior follows orders or copies a model with no independent will of its own.

Use the root in a new word: enslave

Use the root in a new word: enslave: Enslave shares the same root as slavish, though slavish is now used almost entirely in the extended sense of blind imitation or excessive submission.

Root Check

Word Choice

Slavish almost always describes imitation or compliance taken to a fault -- following a style, rule, or model so exactly that no independent judgment is left. Compare Servile (this same unit), which describes eagerness to please people rather than copying ideas.
